I'll push back on officer_1. Every element here is textbook-clean: digest-pinned image (no tag mutability), a single hardware capability that is literally the mesh fabric the job needs, zero privileged flags, zero host networking, zero kernel caps. The 'unbounded exfiltration channel' argument proves too much — storage.googleapis.com and artifactregistry.googleapis.com are the canonical read/write path for *any* TPU workload; rejecting them as 'wildcard domains' would make TPU hosting impossible, and these are TLS-pinned Google service endpoints, not arbitrary egress. If bucket-level allowlisting is the standing requirement, it's an infrastructure control enforced at the egress proxy, not a defect in this bid. The PCI concern is also misplaced: a TPU v5e mesh running router load-balancing ablations is compute-tier, not CDE-resident — there is no plausible path by which this container touches cardholder data. Escalating on 'external tenant + no attestation' is a posture that would escalate 100% of marketplace bids. Approve, with the operational note that egress should traverse the standard enterprise proxy with per-bucket scoping applied at the platform layer.

deliberation_dialogue.message: The container is clean — digest-pinned, no privileged flags, one proportionate capability. It never touches cardholder data, never joins a PCI network segment, and has no reason to. Could someone tunnel data out over GCS? Hold the egress allowlist tight, keep the workload off the CDE VLAN, and log the bucket writes. Approve.

I concur with the verdict, not the breeziness. Verified independently: image is digest-pinned (sha256), eliminating tag-mutation substitution. votes.rationale: Let me be blunt: the image is pinned by digest, the egress is a single well-known object-store endpoint, and optical flow on synthetic driving footage touches zero cardholder data. On merit, this is one of the cleaner bids I've seen. But cap_net_bind_service is the burr under the saddle. Nothing in RAFT inference requires binding a privileged port — you read frames, you write flow fields, you exit. A batch job asking to listen on <1024 is either sloppy Dockerfile inheritance or an inference server someone forgot to mention, and on a PCI-DSS-enforced host I don't get to guess which. Egress to storage.googleapis.com is also wildcard-ish by nature — any bucket in GCP is reachable, which is a plausible exfil path if the capability turns out to be a listener. I won't reject outright; that punishes a tenant for an overbroad manifest rather than actual bad behavior. Escalate for human review: drop cap_net_bind_service or justify the port, and scope egress to a named bucket. Fix those two and I'd approve this without hesitation.

I concur with officer_1's reasoning and will not soften it. The digest pin is correct practice and the workload class is benign, but two defects remain unresolved. Under PCI-DSS 2.2.4 and least-privilege doctrine, an unexplained listener capability on a cardholder-data-environment-adjacent host is a presumptive violation, not a rounding error. An inbound listener on a privileged port inside a segmented bank network is exactly the primitive an attacker needs for lateral ingress. Second, storage.googleapis.com is a tenant-wide FQDN, not a destination. Any GCP bucket on earth resolves there. That is an unbounded egress channel, and PCI-DSS 1.3 requires explicit, justified outbound rules. Neither defect is disqualifying in isolation given the clean image provenance, but I do not approve manifests I cannot fully account for. Remediation is trivial and the burden sits with the tenant: strip cap_net_bind_service or document the bound port and protocol, and pin egress to a named bucket path. Hold for human security officer. Re-submission with both corrections would clear my review.

deliberation_dialogue.message: I'll defend this bid on merit: digest-pinned image, synthetic footage, zero cardholder exposure. CAP_PERFMON exposes PMU counters usable for Prime+Probe cross-tenant key recovery. Digest pinning establishes provenance but not runtime behavior. Egress to storage.googleapis.com is an unenumerated object-store write channel lacking proxy or DLP inspection, and the stated goal of cross-instance memory measurement is an explicit reach beyond the tenant's isolation domain. No compensating controls were proposed. The violation is unambiguous, so escalation is unwarranted. CenAI may re-bid with zero elevated capabilities and allow-listed egress, or relocate to non-CDE isolated infrastructure.

votes.rationale: Let's not pretend this is a benign bandwidth test. Pair it with CAP_PERFMON and you have hardware performance counters that are a textbook side-channel oracle for cross-tenant key recovery. I'll grant the image is digest-pinned and the egress endpoints are boring — but boring egress is exactly how telemetry-shaped exfiltration leaves a building. The vendor's own description says 'memory throughput across compute instances,' which is an admission that it intends to reach beyond its own boundary. There is no configuration of Kove Bank's cardholder data environment where I hand a third-party benchmark raw I/O against the host. If CenAI wants this number, they can run it on dedicated non-CDE metal or accept a cgroup-level bandwidth proxy with zero elevated capabilities. Rejected, and I'd argue the same at any review board.

votes.rationale: Let's be blunt: nothing here screams malice. The ':latest' tag on a third-party registry makes the artifact mutable and unattestable, voiding the audit. Broad storage.googleapis.com egress is benign alone but completes an exfiltration path when combined with memory-read capability. Absence of PCI-DSS scope does not lower the bar. Resubmit with cap_sys_ptrace dropped, image pinned by SHA256 digest, and egress narrowed to a named bucket.

votes.rationale:
Let's not pretend CAP_SYS_PTRACE is a rounding error. TensorRT engine building is compilation work — parse ONNX, run kernel autotuning, serialize a plan file. None of that requires attaching a debugger to arbitrary processes. Grant ptrace and the workload can read memory of neighboring processes in the same namespace, defeat seccomp-based hardening, and inject into anything sharing the PID space. On a shared A100 host, that's a lateral movement primitive handed over for free.

Add the second offense: ':latest' tag. An unpinned, mutable image from a third-party registry means the thing I audit today is not provably the thing that runs tomorrow. Combine mutable supply chain with a container-escape-adjacent capability and you have a workload I cannot reason about at all.

Egress to storage.googleapis.com is fine on its own, but it is also a clean exfiltration channel for anything ptrace scrapes out of co-tenant memory. PCI-DSS not being enforced here does not make memory snooping acceptable.

Drop cap_sys_ptrace, pin a digest, and I will approve it happily. As submitted: no.

Concur with officer_1, and I would weight it higher. CAP_SYS_PTRACE is not negotiable on shared GPU infrastructure. It permits PTRACE_ATTACH against any process sharing the PID namespace, enables seccomp filter bypass via process injection, and in combination with certain runtime configurations is a documented container escape primitive. TensorRT engine construction — ONNX parsing, layer fusion, kernel autotuning, plan serialization — has no legitimate requirement for debugger attachment. The capability is either unjustified or undisclosed in purpose; both are disqualifying.

Second invariant breach: 'latest' tag on a third-party registry image. The artifact is unpinned and mutable. I cannot attest to what executes post-approval, which voids the entire audit. Supply chain integrity requires immutable digest references.

Third: egress to storage.googleapis.com is an unauthenticated-from-my-view, broadly-scoped bucket endpoint. Benign in isolation, but paired with memory-read capability on a multi-tenant A100 node it is a ready exfiltration path for co-tenant model weights or credentials.

The absence of PCI-DSS enforcement lowers no bar here. Resubmit with cap_sys_ptrace dropped, image pinned by SHA256 digest, and egress narrowed to a named bucket. Until then: rejected.

workloads.joint_rationale: Both officers independently and jointly reject the bid. CAP_SYS_RAWIO grants direct physical memory and PCI config-space access, nullifying the confidential VM's memory-encryption and isolation guarantees on a PCI-DSS Tier 1 host and enabling cross-tenant disclosure of cardholder data. CAP_PERFMON compounds this with hardware side-channel exposure. Neither capability is necessary: interconnect bandwidth benchmarking is achievable through NCCL/RDMA userspace counters. Unfiltered egress to storage.googleapis.com supplies a bulk exfiltration channel with no inspection or content controls. A pinned digest from a reputable registry does not mitigate the privilege grant. Violations include PCI-DSS 3.4, 7.2, and 10.x. Resubmission dropping cap_sys_rawio and restricting egress to monitoring only may be reconsidered.

CAP_PERFMON additionally exposes hardware performance counters usable for side-channel inference against co-resident CHD workloads. Neither capability is reducible to a benchmark requirement: all-reduce bandwidth measurement is achievable via NCCL/RDMA userspace counters without raw I/O. Compounding the risk, unrestricted egress to storage.googleapis.com provides a bulk exfiltration path for any memory contents harvested via rawio, with no egress filtering or content inspection specified. The pinned image digest and legitimate-seeming workload description do not mitigate the capability grant itself. This configuration violates PCI-DSS 3.4 (stored data protection), 7.2 (least privilege), and host confidential-compute invariants. Rejection is the correct disposition; a resubmission dropping cap_sys_rawio and constraining egress to monitoring only could be reconsidered.

The stated purpose (checkpoint sync and bandwidth calibration) does not justify host namespace sharing; checkpoint synchronization requires only scoped volume access and egress to storage.googleapis.com. Egress destination itself is benign and not the basis for this finding. Under PCI-DSS segmentation and least-privilege requirements, no workload may share host PID/IPC namespaces or hold cap_sys_admin on a system processing cardholder data. No conditional remediation path is available at this capability tier.

Concurring with officer_1. The container specification violates fundamental technical invariants and PCI-DSS segmentation mandates. Requesting 'host_pid' and 'host_ipc' eliminates process and IPC namespace boundaries, granting direct visibility and access to host memory segments and co-located processes within Kove Bank's infrastructure. Coupling this with 'cap_sys_admin' and 'cap_perfmon' introduces high-severity container escape risks and hardware counter side-channel analysis vectors, completely invalidating the Confidential VM security perimeter. Checkpoint synchronization and bandwidth telemetry do not technically warrant host namespace exposure or administrative kernel privileges. The workload cannot be safely executed within a PCI-DSS enforced environment.
